resultJson.description:
HUE_PSK is the pre-shared key for the DTLS entertainment stream to the Hue bridge. Today it is a plain `String` in `HueCredentials`, and `DtlsEmitter` decodes it lazily with `ByteVector.fromHex(creds.psk).getOrElse(ByteVector.empty)`. That has two problems. A typo, stray quote or empty value quietly turns into an empty key and only shows up later as an unrelated handshake failure. And scodec's `fromHex` is lenient: it accepts a `0x` prefix and skips whitespace and underscores inside the key.

This epic makes the key a validated type that is checked when the config loads. A key is valid if, after trimming surrounding whitespace, it is exactly 32 hex digits in any case. The shared contract changes from `HueCredentials.psk: String` to a decoded, redacted key type built through a smart constructor and read by a pureconfig `ConfigReader`. Its failure message names HUE_PSK, says it must be 32 hex digits, and never includes the value. `DtlsEmitter` then uses the already-decoded bytes, so the empty-key fallback goes away. The other credentials and the handshake itself stay as they are.

`Main` gets a small startup seam so the startup behaviour can be tested. It runs from a given `ConfigSource`. When the config is rejected, it logs the pureconfig failures, which carry the reason and never the value, and returns `ExitCode.Error`. This happens before anything is built: no HTTP client, no Spotify callback server on 7070, no Hue request, no DTLS connector. `IOApp` already exits non-zero when `run` raises, so the catch exists only to make the exit status observable through `start`. It also deliberately applies to every config failure (a missing Spotify key, a bad palette name), which now gets a logged error and `ExitCode.Error` instead of a stack trace.

tasks.title: Validated Hue PSK type, read and checked when the config loads
tasks.description: Add `src/main/scala/domain/hue/Psk.scala` (package `domain.hue`, brace syntax). Make it `final case class Psk private (bytes: ByteVector)`, built only through `Psk.parse(raw: String): Either[String, Psk]`. Don't use an opaque type over ByteVector: `ByteVector.toString` prints the hex. `parse` trims the input, then requires exactly `[0-9a-fA-F]{32}`. Check with that regex: don't validate with `ByteVector.fromHex`, which accepts `0x` and skips internal whitespace and underscores. Decode only after the check passes. The Left message names HUE_PSK and says it must be 32 hex digits (e.g. "HUE_PSK must be 32 hex digits"), with no part of the input. Override `toString` to something like `Psk(<redacted>)`. Keep the case class's structural equality, because `LightShowConfigSpec` compares whole `AppConfig`s. Lint trap: Scalafix `CaseClassExplicitCopy` is a lint error and targets case classes with a private constructor that don't declare `copy`/`apply`. Add a `private def copy` (and a private `apply` if the rule asks for it), and run `sbt lint` as soon as the file compiles rather than finding out at the end. Put a `given ConfigReader[Psk]` in the companion: `ConfigReader[String].emap(s => Psk.parse(s).left.map(UserValidationFailed(_)))`, or use a custom `FailureReason` whose `description` is the message. Never use `CannotConvert`, because its description embeds the value. Change `HueCredentials.psk` to `Psk`. In `client/DtlsEmitter.scala`, change line 23 to `creds.psk.bytes.toArray` (no fallback) and remove the then-unused `scodec.bits.ByteVector` import (line 14). Touch nothing else in that file. Update the six fixtures with short PSKs to a made-up valid 32-digit key: `"00ff"` in LightsSpec:23, HueClientSpec:14 and SyncEngineRunSpec:32; HOCON `psk = "00ff"` in LightShowConfigSpec:11 and SettingsJsonSpec:29; and `"HUE_PSK" -> "00"` in LightShowConfigSpec:81. Tests: a new `src/test/scala/domain/hue/PskSpec.scala` with ScalaCheck properties, plus config-load cases that go through `ConfigSource.string(...)` with the `reference.conf` fallback, using both `.load[AppConfig]` and `AppConfig.load[IO]`. Put the load cases next to the existing ones in `LightShowConfigSpec` or in a new `domain/config/HueConfigSpec.scala`. They must show that: 32 hex digits in upper, lower or mixed case are accepted and decode to the same bytes; leading or trailing spaces and a newline are accepted; empty, 31 digits, 33 digits, a non-hex character (e.g. `g`), a `0x` prefix, a quote inside and a space inside are each rejected when the config loads; the error (`prettyPrint()` and the raised `ConfigReaderException`'s `getMessage`) names HUE_PSK and says "32 hex digits"; and the error contains neither the value nor any 4+ character substring of it. Build every bad input from hex digits plus the single offending part, so that no innocent 4-character run collides with the fixed error text (`hue.creds.psk`, the origin, the message words). The rejected input, empty value aside, should also never appear in the error. Also update README.md's env table row for `HUE_PSK` to say it is 32 hex digits, and tick the 'Fail fast on a bad Hue key' item in `docs/roadmap.md`. Leave docs/how-it-works.md alone. Run `sbt fix` then `sbt check`.

tasks.title: Main stops at startup with a failure exit code when the config is rejected
tasks.description: In `src/main/scala/Main.scala`, move the body of `run` into `def start(source: ConfigSource): IO[ExitCode]`, and make `run` call `start(ConfigSource.default)`. Load the config first, as now, before the TLS context, Ember client, `SpotifyClient.resource`, `HueClient` or `DtlsEmitter`. Recover a `pureconfig.error.ConfigReaderException` from `AppConfig.load` by logging `e.failures.prettyPrint()` inline at error level and returning `ExitCode.Error`. Don't add a helper outside Main: Main is excluded from coverage, and the message content is already tested at config level. This is a deliberate change for every config failure, not just the PSK. `IOApp` would already exit non-zero on the raised error, and the catch exists to make the exit status testable through `start`. Leave the rest of the wiring alone. Add `src/test/scala/MainSpec.scala` (a `CatsEffectSuite`). It calls `Main.start` with `ConfigSource.string(...)` with a `ConfigSource.resources("reference.conf")` fallback and dummy Spotify values. It covers a non-hex HUE_PSK, an empty one, 31 and 33 digits, a `0x` prefix, a quote inside and a space inside, and asserts `ExitCode.Error` for each. To show that no bridge connection is attempted, set `hue.creds.address` to `127.0.0.1:<port>` of a raw TCP listener: `fs2.io.net.Network[IO].serverResource` on an ephemeral port, counting accepted sockets in a `Ref` and closing each one at once. Assert the count is zero. It has to be a socket counter, not an HTTP fake that counts requests: `HueClient` talks HTTPS, so a plain HTTP fake never sees a readable request even when the app did connect. Without the change, a bad key gets past config, binds the Spotify callback port 7070, then `Lights.fromBridge` connects to the listener, and that is what makes the test fail. To cover criterion 6 (no output at startup contains the key), capture log events in the test with a logback `ListAppender` attached to the root logger for the duration of each case (logback-classic is already on the classpath). Assert that a startup error was logged naming HUE_PSK and that no logged message contains a 4+ character substring of the key. Build the bad keys as in the config tests (hex digits plus the offending part) so the fixed text can't collide. Run `sbt fix` then `sbt check`.

resultJson.brief:
Modules: `root` (`.`, the app: src/main/scala, has pureconfig, scodec-bits, http4s Ember, fs2-io, log4cats with logback-classic, Californium Scandium), `model/` (cross JVM/JS settings and colours, no pureconfig, not touched here), `ui/` (Scala.js settings page, not touched).

Key files:
- `src/main/scala/domain/hue/HueCredentials.scala`: `case class HueCredentials(address: String, username: String, psk: String)`. This is the contract that changes. It has no explicit reader: `HueConfig` (`src/main/scala/domain/config/HueConfig.scala`, `case class HueConfig(creds: HueCredentials, zoneId: Option[String] = None) derives ConfigReader`) derives through it, and a `given ConfigReader[Psk]` in `Psk`'s companion is picked up by that derivation.
- `src/main/scala/domain/config/AppConfig.scala`: `AppConfig.load[F[_]: Sync](source: ConfigSource): F[AppConfig] = Sync[F].blocking(source.loadOrThrow[AppConfig])`, which raises `pureconfig.error.ConfigReaderException[AppConfig]`. `.failures.prettyPrint()` and getMessage read like \"Cannot convert configuration to a ... Failures are: at 'hue.creds.psk': - (origin) <description>\". Only the FailureReason's `description` appears there, so use `UserValidationFailed(msg)` or a custom FailureReason, never `CannotConvert(value, ...)`, which prints the value.
- `src/main/scala/domain/config/LightShowConfigReaders.scala`: shows the reader style (`ConfigReader[String].emap { ... .toRight(...) }`).
- `src/main/resources/application.conf`: `hue.creds.psk = ${HUE_PSK}` (env substitution; the value keeps surrounding whitespace or a newline, so `parse` trims). `reference.conf` holds the light-show defaults.
- `src/main/scala/client/DtlsEmitter.scala` (colon-indented legacy file, excluded from coverage): line 23 `private lazy val pskBytes = ByteVector.fromHex(creds.psk).getOrElse(ByteVector.empty).toArray` feeds `new AdvancedSinglePskStore(creds.username, pskBytes)`. The `ByteVector` import on line 14 is used only there. scodec's `fromHex` accepts `0x` and skips whitespace and underscores, so it is not a validator.
- `src/main/scala/client/HueClient.scala:19`: `baseUri = Uri.unsafeFromString(s\"https://${creds.address}/clip/v2\")`. The bridge is always reached over HTTPS, and an address like `127.0.0.1:12345` targets a local port.
- `src/main/scala/client/SpotifyClient.scala:148-156`: `SpotifyClient.resource` binds an Ember callback server on 127.0.0.1:7070 and doesn't contact Spotify until later.
- `src/main/scala/Main.scala`: `object Main extends IOApp`. `run` is one `Resource` for-comprehension. Its first step is `Resource.eval(AppConfig.load[IO](pureconfig.ConfigSource.default))`, followed by `TLSContext.Builder.forAsync[IO].insecure`, the Ember client, `SpotifyClient.resource`, `HueClient`, `DtlsEmitter`, then `Lights.fromBridge(hueClient)` (the first Hue request), and so on. Logging is `Slf4jLogger.getLogger[IO]`. Main is excluded from coverage (`coverageExcludedPackages` in build.sbt:92) and has no tests yet.
- Test fixtures with short PSKs that become invalid: `src/test/scala/LightsSpec.scala:23`, `client/HueClientSpec.scala:14` and `SyncEngineRunSpec.scala:32` (`\"00ff\"`); `domain/config/LightShowConfigSpec.scala:11` and `domain/config/SettingsJsonSpec.scala:29` (`psk = \"00ff\"` in HOCON); and `LightShowConfigSpec.scala:81` (`\"HUE_PSK\" -> \"00\"`). LightShowConfigSpec loads through `ConfigSource.string(required + x).withFallback(ConfigSource.resources(\"reference.conf\")).load[AppConfig].left.map(_.prettyPrint())`, which is a good pattern for config-level tests. Its first test compares whole `AppConfig`s, so the PSK type needs value equality (ByteVector, not Array).
- Docs: README.md:27 env table row `HUE_PSK`, and docs/roadmap.md:8, which lists this exact item.

Conventions (CLAUDE.md and .scalafix.conf):
- Scala 3 brace syntax in new code; `given`/`using`/`summon`, no `implicit` or `implicitly`. Public defs and givens have explicit types. The file name matches the type, and the package matches the directory (FileNameConsistent and DirectoryAndPackageName are lint errors).
- `CaseClassExplicitCopy` is a lint error: a case class with a private constructor needs explicit (private) `copy`/`apply`. Check with `sbt lint` early.
- Typed failures: smart constructors return `Either`, errors are raised in `F`, and code never matches on `getMessage`. No `unsafeRun*` or global runtime outside Main (DisableSyntax). Tests follow `.scalafix.test.conf`, and `CatsEffectSuite` tests return their IO.
- Make the smallest change at the point of the problem; don't reformat or reshape working code (leave DtlsEmitter's colon syntax). Comment only what code can't say.
- Tests: munit plus munit-scalacheck properties, `CatsEffectSuite` (munit-cats-effect 2.0.0), `TestControl` for timing. External services are faked over HTTP (`Client.fromHttpApp(HttpRoutes.of[IO]{...}.orNotFound)`) or with local servers. No comments in tests; the test name says what it checks. `src/test/resources/logback-test.xml` sends WARN+ to stdout on the root logger.
- Finish with `sbt fix`, then `sbt check` (lint, tests with coverage: 90% statements and 85% branches overall, 70% statements per file). Never lower the thresholds, widen the exclusions or disable rules.
- Secrets: never print or log `.env` or any real key. Test keys are made-up hex.
